question: The first computer to run a business's routine office work, in 1951, was built by what kind of company?
answer: A tea-shop chain. J. Lyons & Co., which ran hundreds of teashops and bakeries on thin margins, built LEO I itself after studying early computers in America and Cambridge. From late 1951 it valued the bakeries' weekly output. Lyons went on to sell LEO computers to other firms.
move: The first users of a tool are those with the most tedious volume.
trap: A bank, since banks had the most sums to do.
reference: Ferry, A Computer Called LEO: Lyons Tea Shops and the World's First Office Computer, Fourth Estate, 2003
